title: The Rain That Filled Every Granary
text: In the year 110 the Oracle spoke: Magavik and Dazawail had empty granaries while Wasir and Nohohosh slept on full stores, and unless the valley shared its bread, hunger would cut the people down to fewer than 286. The valley grew instead. Haitoul sent forty people away to found Touzun in 115, and forty more to found Daasou in 133. Hunger came only once, in 126, and it struck Nohohosh, one of the well-fed tribes, taking three lives. In 132 the god faced the dilemma of the Three Hungry Hearths and sent rain over the whole valley, choosing no favorites, and the fields of every tribe were watered. When the time ran out in 135, 411 people lived across seven tribes, far above the number the Oracle had foretold, and the prophecy was broken. Still, Magavik holds only a third of a month's food and Nohohosh less than one month, so the hunger has not gone away.
causes: The god sent rain to the whole valley in 132, so every tribe's fields were watered, not just one tribe's
The only famine, in 126, took just 3 lives in Nohohosh, so the population never shrank toward 285
The valley kept growing until it held 411 people in seven tribes, with Touzun and Daasou founded by people from Haitoul
